Title: Diagnosis
Details: 
The failing test `testToClass_object()` calls `ClassUtils.toClass(Object[])` with an array containing a String, null, and a Double: `new Object[] { "Test", null, 99d }`. The test expects the resulting Class array to be `[String.class, null, Double.class]`.

Examining the implementation of `ClassUtils.toClass(Object[])` reveals the cause of the failure. The method iterates over the input array, and for each element calls `array[i].getClass()`, storing the result in a `Class<?>` array. However, if an element in the array is `null`, then calling `getClass()` on that element will throw a `NullPointerException`.

Thus, when the method encounters the `null` element at index 1, it throws an NPE, causing the test to fail.

The current bug report summarizes this as "`toClass(Object[])` throws NPE on null array element", which is exactly the behavior observed.

There are no clues from the recent bug reports that relate to this specific issue.

The root cause is that the `toClass` method does not handle null elements in the input array gracefully and directly calls `getClass()` on each element without a null check.

In the test, the expected behavior is that the output array should have `null` in the corresponding position if the input element is `null`.

To fix this issue, the method should check if the element is `null`. If so, it should put `null` in the corresponding index of the classes array instead of calling `getClass()`.

This explains the failure and the root cause accurately.
org.apache.commons.lang3.ClassUtils.toClass(java.lang.Object[])
